ns2:section.sectionText: Prerequisites: One of TAM 470, ME 471, AAE 420, CEE 570, or CS 455 or equivalent Objectives: This course is intended to serve as a sequel to an introductory finite element course, such as AAE 420, CEE 570, or ME 471 or a survey numerical methods course such as TAM 470. It is designed to deepen the students understanding of the mathematical background of the finite element method and to introduce topics that are typically not covered in a first course. Among the topics to be covered are: an introduction to functional analysis and other mathematical theory that supports the finite element method, FEM for elliptic and parabolic equations, error estimates, adaptive analysis, C1 finite elements, nonconforming finite finite elements, and mixed finite element methods for the Poisson and the Stokes equations. Applications to problems of current interest in mechanics and other sciences will be developed. We will also look at computational examples using the FEniCS finite element software environment.
